Four squads guard him while believers pray continually. On the night before his expected public appearance, Peter sleeps chained between soldiers. An angel wakes him, his chains fall away, and he follows the angel past guards and through an opening iron gate.

At first Peter thinks he is dreaming. Once outside, he recognizes his escape and goes to Mary's house, where believers are praying. The servant Rhoda recognizes his voice but is so excited that she forgets to open the door. Others reject her report until Peter's continued knocking brings them to him. He describes the rescue, asks them to inform James and the others, and leaves. Herod later orders the guards' execution.

In Caesarea, Herod addresses people seeking reconciliation after a dispute involving their food supply. They acclaim his voice as divine. Acts describes an angel striking him because he does not give God the glory; he dies after being consumed by worms. In contrast, God's message continues spreading. The passage ends with Barnabas, Saul, and John Mark together after their service.

stories.title: Paul's First Journey
stories.summary:
During worship and fasting at Antioch, the Holy Spirit directs the community to set apart Barnabas and Saul. They travel to Cyprus with John as their helper. At Paphos, the official Sergius Paulus wants to hear their message, but Elymas opposes them. Saul, also called Paul, announces that Elymas will temporarily lose his sight. The official believes after witnessing what happens.

John leaves them at Perga. In Pisidian Antioch, Paul addresses a synagogue, tracing Israel's history toward Jesus. He proclaims Jesus' resurrection and forgiveness through him. Interest spreads, but opposition leads Paul and Barnabas to direct their message toward Gentiles. They are expelled and travel to Iconium, where a divided response again brings threats.

In Lystra, Paul heals a man unable to walk since birth. The crowd mistakes the missionaries for gods and prepares sacrifices. Paul and Barnabas insist that they are human and call the people toward the living Creator. Opponents later turn the crowd against Paul. He is stoned and dragged outside as if dead, but rises and continues to Derbe.

The pair then retrace their route, encouraging disciples to endure hardship and appointing community elders with prayer and fasting. They return to their sending community in Antioch and report the opening of faith among the Gentiles.

stories.title: The Jerusalem Council
stories.summary:
A dispute arises at Antioch when visitors insist that Gentile believers must be circumcised to be saved. Paul and Barnabas strongly disagree and travel with others to Jerusalem for discussion with the apostles and elders. Some believers from the Pharisees maintain that Gentiles must receive circumcision and keep the law of Moses.

Peter recalls that God gave the Holy Spirit to Gentiles without distinguishing them from Jewish believers. He argues against placing on them a burden that previous generations could not bear. Salvation, he says, comes through Jesus' grace for both groups. Barnabas and Paul describe signs among the nations. James then cites prophetic words about Gentiles seeking the Lord.

James proposes not troubling Gentile converts with the disputed requirements. Instead, they should avoid food associated with idols, blood, meat from strangled animals, and sexual immorality. The assembly agrees and sends a letter with Paul, Barnabas, Judas Barsabbas, and Silas. It states that the troubling demands had not been authorized and presents the agreed instructions.

At Antioch, the community rejoices at the letter's encouragement. Judas and Silas further strengthen them with teaching. Paul and Barnabas remain there, continuing their work alongside others.

stories.title: Paul in Philippi
stories.summary:
Paul recruits Timothy at Lystra and circumcises him because local Jewish communities know his father is Greek. They deliver the Jerusalem decisions and strengthen churches along the route. After the Spirit prevents travel into certain regions, Paul sees a vision of a Macedonian asking for help. The group crosses to Macedonia and reaches Philippi.

At a riverside prayer gathering, Lydia, a merchant in purple cloth, responds to Paul's teaching. She and her household receive baptism, and she welcomes the travelers into her home. Later, an enslaved girl repeatedly follows them, identifying them as God's servants. Paul commands the divining spirit to leave her. Her owners, deprived of their income, have Paul and Silas dragged before the magistrates. They are beaten and imprisoned.

At midnight, while they pray and sing, an earthquake opens the prison doors and loosens the chains. The jailer fears the prisoners have escaped, but Paul stops him from harming himself. He hears their message, tends their wounds, and receives baptism with his household.

The next morning, officials order a quiet release. Paul protests that Roman citizens were publicly beaten without trial. The magistrates come personally and request their departure. Paul and Silas encourage the believers at Lydia's house before leaving.

stories.title: Thessalonica, Athens and Corinth
stories.summary:
In Thessalonica, Paul argues from scripture that the Messiah had to suffer and rise, identifying Jesus with that promise. Some listeners join him, but opponents stir up a crowd and accuse his supporters of disloyalty to Caesar. Paul and Silas leave for Berea, where people examine scripture daily. Further agitation drives Paul onward to Athens.

Disturbed by Athens's idols, Paul speaks in the synagogue and marketplace. At the Areopagus, he uses an altar to an unknown god as his starting point. He describes the Creator as the giver of life, beyond temples and images, and calls for repentance before a coming judgment. His reference to resurrection draws mockery, curiosity, and some belief.

In Corinth, Paul works with fellow tentmakers Aquila and Priscilla. He teaches for eighteen months, encouraged by a vision promising protection. Opponents bring him before Gallio, who refuses to adjudicate their religious dispute. Sosthenes is beaten before the tribunal without Gallio intervening.

Paul later travels with Aquila and Priscilla to Ephesus, then continues toward Caesarea and Antioch before another journey of encouragement. In Ephesus, the learned speaker Apollos teaches about Jesus but knows only John's baptism. Aquila and Priscilla explain the message more fully. Apollos then goes to Achaia, helping believers and arguing from scripture that Jesus is the Messiah.

stories.title: Ephesus
stories.summary:
In Ephesus, Paul meets about twelve disciples who know John's baptism but have not heard of the Holy Spirit. They receive baptism in Jesus' name, and the Spirit comes upon them when Paul lays hands on them. He teaches first in the synagogue and later in Tyrannus's lecture hall. His work continues for two years, with healings and a growing audience across the province.

Some traveling exorcists attempt to use Jesus' name without Paul's relationship to him. A possessed man overpowers them, and fear spreads. Many converts publicly burn costly magical books. A silversmith named Demetrius then rallies craftsmen whose trade in Artemis shrines is threatened by Paul's teaching. A confused crowd fills the theater. The city clerk eventually disperses it, insisting that complaints belong in lawful proceedings.

After traveling through Macedonia and Greece, Paul visits Troas. During a long evening talk, Eutychus falls asleep in a window and drops from the third floor. He is picked up dead, but Paul embraces him and assures the gathering that he lives. The community is comforted.

At Miletus, Paul summons the Ephesian elders for a farewell. He recalls his service, warns of future dangers within and outside the community, and urges care for the vulnerable. Expecting suffering in Jerusalem, he entrusts them to God. They pray and weep before accompanying him to the ship.

stories.title: Paul Arrested in Jerusalem
stories.summary:
On his journey to Jerusalem, Paul receives repeated warnings. At Tyre, disciples urge him not to continue. In Caesarea, the prophet Agabus binds himself with Paul's belt to portray Paul's coming arrest. His companions plead with him, but he says he is ready to suffer and die for Jesus.

In Jerusalem, Paul reports his work among Gentiles to James and the elders. To answer rumors that he rejects Jewish customs, they ask him to join four men in purification and pay their expenses. While he is in the temple, visitors from Asia accuse him of teaching against the people, law, and temple. They also wrongly assume he has brought a Gentile inside. A crowd attacks him until Roman soldiers intervene.

Allowed to address the crowd, Paul recounts his Jewish education, persecution of believers, encounter with Jesus near Damascus, and commissioning. His reference to being sent to Gentiles renews the uproar. A planned interrogation by flogging stops when he asserts Roman citizenship.

Before the council, Paul's declaration about resurrection divides Pharisees and Sadducees. Soldiers again remove him for protection. That night, Jesus assures him that he will testify in Rome. More than forty men plot an ambush, but Paul's nephew informs the commander. Paul is transferred under heavy escort to Caesarea, where Governor Felix keeps him in custody pending his accusers' arrival.

stories.title: Paul Before Felix, Festus and Agrippa
stories.summary:
Before Governor Felix, Paul's accusers portray him as a public agitator who tried to defile the temple. Paul denies creating unrest and says he came with offerings and aid for his people. He acknowledges following the Way and believing in resurrection, but challenges his accusers to support their claims. Felix postpones a decision and allows visitors to help him. Over two years, he repeatedly hears Paul while hoping for a bribe.

Festus succeeds Felix and hears renewed accusations. When he suggests moving the hearing to Jerusalem, Paul appeals to Caesar. Festus accepts the appeal but struggles to identify a clear charge for the emperor. King Agrippa and Bernice visit, providing an occasion for another hearing.

Paul describes his former life as a strict Pharisee and his violent persecution of Jesus' followers. He recounts the heavenly appearance near Damascus and Jesus' commission to bring light and forgiveness to others. He insists that his message of suffering and resurrection follows Moses and the prophets.

Festus calls him mad, but Paul defends the reasonableness of his testimony and appeals directly to Agrippa. He wishes his hearers could share his faith without his chains. Afterward, the rulers agree that he has done nothing deserving death or imprisonment. Agrippa says he could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar.

stories.title: Shipwreck and Rome
stories.summary:
Paul sails toward Italy as a prisoner under the officer Julius. Contrary winds slow the journey. Despite Paul's warning, the ship leaves Crete and is caught in a prolonged storm. Cargo and equipment are thrown overboard as hope fades. Paul reports an angel's promise that he must appear before Caesar and that everyone aboard will survive, though the ship will be lost.

As land approaches, Paul prevents the sailors from abandoning the ship and urges everyone to eat. The vessel runs aground and breaks apart. Julius stops soldiers from killing the prisoners, and all 276 people reach shore by swimming or holding wreckage.

On Malta, residents welcome the survivors with a fire. A viper fastens onto Paul's hand, but he shakes it off unharmed. He heals the father of Publius and other sick islanders. After three months, the group sails onward, eventually reaching Rome. Fellow believers meet Paul along the way and encourage him.

In Rome, Paul lives under a soldier's guard and explains his case to local Jewish leaders. A later gathering hears his arguments about Jesus from the law and prophets. Responses divide. Paul cites Isaiah concerning resistant hearing and declares that God's salvation is also going to the nations. Acts ends with two years in rented quarters, where he welcomes visitors and teaches openly about God's kingdom and Jesus.
